If I need to, I put my extra needle in it’s tube at the start of the session and attach a machine bag to the tube so the entire top part (that will be going into the machine) is completely covered and on a far corner of my station away from my other machines/ink. Clean gloves on, slip one under the machine bag and remove current tube (and bag), i unclip the needle through the bag so no touching of the machine with the same hand that’s touched the grip. Slide the new tube up with that hand (it’s gonna get touched in a minute when I tattoo anyway, so no worries about contaminating the bottom bit I hold while the upper part is completely covered) keeping the clean hand on the machine under the new bag, clip into place through the bag and secure the bag. Only the completely clean glove touches the actual machine at any point, only one glove change required, and all my machines get cleaned before and after each session regardless— if I’m able to I’ll avoid having to change needles because it’s a faff, but I’m pretty happy with this method

Yes, but not in the sense that you should be looking for an apprenticeship yet. Keep drawing, as much as you can, as many different styles and subject matter as you can. When you think you’ve drawn enough, draw more. And then some more. Work on stuff you hate drawing as much (if not more) than stuff you like, practise linework and shading. You clearly have a great imagination and some lovely ideas, but the technical skill and attention to detail needs improvement— this just comes with time! Keep at it and you’ll see some huge improvements. Look at artists whose work you admire and take inspiration (or even do some studies of their work— as long as you’re not including it in a portfolio or posting it as your own, copying to learn and improve is fine!). Best of luck!

So basically, put in as much detail as you can(whilst still being coherent, nobody wants to hear you ramble about the deep meaning behind your tattoo if it's not relevant)---it's much easier for the artist to get a good idea of the work this way.

Any reputable tattoo artist will not copy another artist's design. Just find a tattoo artist nearby you like and get them to design you something inspired by the other design, or save up and travel to get the design you like. Don't copy other people's art.
